label: Naloxone — competitive opioid (mu) antagonism

extraction.tier_rationale: Competitive mu-antagonism shifts the opioid's apparent Ce50; the Ki is illustrative (Tier-C). The CLINICAL point is the renarcotization failure mode, which is robust.

known_failure_modes.condition: reversing a longer-acting opioid (antagonist clears first)
known_failure_modes.behavior: naloxone's half-life (~60-90 min) is SHORTER than most opioids it reverses (e.g. fentanyl/morphine); as naloxone washes out the receptor block wanes and respiratory depression / sedation RELAPSES (renarcotization) -- the antidote outlasted by the agonist.

extraction.tier_rationale: Competitive-antagonist exemplar; the renarcotization relapse is the load-bearing, safety-relevant forward behavior (the antagonist clears before the agonist). Disposition values textbook, Ki illustrative.

notes: Competitive reversal: the apparent-Ce50 multiplier (1 + C_naloxone/Ki) rises then FALLS back toward 1 as naloxone clears -> the opioid effect relapses (renarcotization), rendered as honest forward output, never a re-dosing schedule.
